name: The Holm Oak of Villa Fondi

location.address: Villa Fondi De Sangro, Via Ripa di Cassano, Piano di Sorrento
location.neighbourhood: Piano di Sorrento (adjoining Sorrento, on the peninsula)

verified_sources: data/research/sorrento-register-candidates.json (Italy MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 14/G568/NA/15)
access: Free, public municipal park (Villa Fondi De Sangro, owned by the Comune di Piano di Sorrento, houses the Georges Vallet archaeological museum). Open as a public park; no permission needed to walk the grounds.
transport: Circumvesuviana train from Sorrento station to Piano di Sorrento station (one stop, a few minutes), then about 10 minutes on foot via Via Ripa di Cassano.
verify_notes: Two independent official sources: Italy's national MASAF monumental-trees register (girth 318cm, height 11m, coords 40.637722/14.401725) and the Regione Campania's own tree card (scheda_64, girth 318cm, height 11m matching exactly, age ~150 years, coords 40.637222/14.401389). The two sources' coordinates disagree by roughly 60-70 metres, both well within the small Villa Fondi park grounds, so location_precision is set approximate (park-level) rather than confirmed (tree-level) despite two sources; used the MASAF register's coordinate as primary. Regione Campania source: age approximated at 150 years, planted around the time the villa's garden was first laid out in 1875 (so the tree itself may be somewhat younger than the garden). Villa built 1840 by Giovanni Andrea De Sangro, Prince of Fondi; acquired by the Comune di Piano di Sorrento and restored in the 1990s as a museum/park. No vitality concerns found for this specific tree in web coverage (the WWF/Soprintendenza alarm and dendrosurgery coverage found elsewhere concerns the villa's stone pine, not this oak). Worth the walk for the view over the Bay of Naples and Vesuvius alongside the archaeological museum.

name: The Stone Pine of Villa Fondi

location.address: Villa Fondi De Sangro, Via Ripa di Cassano 26-34, Piano di Sorrento
location.neighbourhood: Piano di Sorrento (adjoining Sorrento, on the peninsula)

verified_sources: data/research/sorrento-register-candidates.json (Italy MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 01/G568/NA/15)
access: Free, public municipal park (Villa Fondi De Sangro, owned by the Comune di Piano di Sorrento, houses the Georges Vallet archaeological museum). Open as a public park; no permission needed to walk the grounds.
transport: Circumvesuviana train from Sorrento station to Piano di Sorrento station (one stop, a few minutes), then about 10 minutes on foot via Via Ripa di Cassano.
verify_notes: Two independent official sources agree tightly: MASAF national register (girth 418cm, height 20m, coords 40.637314/14.401667) and Regione Campania's own tree card (scheda_29, girth 418cm, height 20.0m, coords 40.637251/14.401671, about 7m apart, tree-level agreement). Regione Campania text: age approximated at 150 years, presumably dating to the villa garden's first planting in 1875. Flagged for vitality: a 2020 Positanonews piece describing the villa's garden (by Prof. Antonio Volpe) mentions a large pine on the western, sea-facing side of the garden, roughly 200 years old, damaged by Scolytidae bark beetles (genus Pinus) and treated with dendrosurgery to save it; it is not certain this is the exact same tree as the registered specimen (the article says Pinus pinaster in one summarised extract, register says Pinus pinea, so species citation may be imprecise in the secondary source, or the garden holds more than one old pine). Separately, a 2014 WWF alarm (reported by SorrentoPress/politicainpenisola.it) said Villa Fondi's pines were 'the last surviving specimens in the urban area on the tufaceous slope of Piano di Sorrento' and objected to drastic pruning; the Soprintendenza confirmed the villa and its park trees are a protected site and blocked cutting. No source states the registered pine has died or been removed; TripAdvisor visitor reviews of the villa/park are recent (2023-2024), consistent with the park and its trees still standing. Worth the walk alongside the Holm Oak for the sea view and the archaeological museum.

name: The Cemetery Cypress of Piano di Sorrento

location.address: Cimitero Comunale, Via Gennaro Maresca 84, Piano di Sorrento
location.neighbourhood: Piano di Sorrento (adjoining Sorrento, on the peninsula)

verified_sources: data/research/sorrento-register-candidates.json (Italy MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 05/G568/NA/15)
access: Free, public municipal cemetery, open daily during standard daylight hours set by the Comune di Piano di Sorrento (exact hours vary seasonally and around 1/6 January; check locally). No permission needed to enter.
transport: Circumvesuviana train from Sorrento station to Piano di Sorrento station, then about 15 minutes on foot uphill via Via Gennaro Maresca.
verify_notes: Two independent official sources: MASAF national register (girth 266cm, height 10m, coords 40.628472/14.418836) and Regione Campania's tree card (scheda_38, girth 266cm, height 10.0m matching exactly, coords 40.628097/14.417969, roughly 90m from the MASAF point, both within the cemetery grounds), so set approximate rather than confirmed despite the girth match. Regione Campania text: based on verbal testimony, planted in 1876, the year the Cimitero Comunale opened, giving a presumed age of over 130 years (in 2020; roughly 150 now). Two further cypresses (girths 270cm and 325cm per MASAF, sheet ids 06/G568/NA/15 and 04/G568/NA/15) stand elsewhere in the same cemetery but were not found with a second independent source in this pass; recorded as leads rather than shipped. The cemetery is a public, free, everyday municipal facility, no different in kind from a churchyard.

name: The Plane Tree of Via Maresca

location.address: Via Gennaro Maresca, corner Via Formiello, Piano di Sorrento
location.neighbourhood: Piano di Sorrento (adjoining Sorrento, on the peninsula)

verified_sources: data/research/sorrento-register-candidates.json (Italy MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 07/G568/NA/15)
access: Free, standing on a public street corner. Visible and reachable at any time.
transport: Circumvesuviana train from Sorrento station to Piano di Sorrento station, then about 12 minutes on foot via Via Gennaro Maresca (on the way up to the cemetery).
verify_notes: Two independent official sources agree tightly: MASAF national register (girth 295cm, height 10m, coords 40.629217/14.417128) and Regione Campania's tree card (scheda_40, girth 295cm, height 10.0m matching exactly, coords 40.629168/14.417120, about 5m apart, tree-level agreement). Regione Campania text: planted around 1920 per local verbal testimony, presumed age about 100 years (as of the 2020 update; roughly 105-110 now). Stands on a curve of the steep municipal road up to the cemetery, described by the register as a long-standing shade landmark for passers-by and a wayfinding point on the second-to-last bend before the cemetery; it stands beside a second, smaller-girth plane tree, and this registered one is the more imposing of the pair. Crown described as free of degenerated branch stubs (a vitality-positive note) as of the register's last update (2020).
